input.text: Where heaven got a circle, earth got a square. Ditan, the Temple of Earth, was built in the fifteen thirties as the counterpart to the Temple of Heaven — and for nearly five centuries, emperors came here each summer solstice to sacrifice to the Earth deity from this stark square stone terrace, the largest of its kind. Today it's a beloved park of old cypresses, and the city's most famous temple fair ground: every Spring Festival, Ditan hosts Beijing's biggest fair — lion dances, folk crafts, snack stalls in a happy crush of locals. The literary-minded know it from a beloved essay, "I and Ditan" by the writer Shi Tiesheng, who spent years in these alleys thinking about fate after illness — the park remembers him fondly. Quiet on ordinary days, roaring at New Year — Ditan is heaven's mirror and Beijing's living room.
